title: Hopping on a number line
examples: Teacher, if I start at 5 and hop forward 2, what number do I land on?
Can we practice counting back from 10?
What is the difference between counting on and counting back?

explain.say: Today we are going to hop numbers on a number line. This helps us count forwards and backwards.
To count on, you start at a number and add more. Imagine hopping forward on the line.
Now let us count back. This means we take away numbers. We hop backward on the line.
If you start at 10 and hop back 2, you land on 8. You are counting backwards.
In real life, counting on helps us know how many more cookies we can eat. If we have three and eat two more, we have five.
A common mistake is forgetting to move the whole amount. If we start at five and count on three, we must count all three hops.

faq.q: What is the difference between counting on and counting back?
faq.a: Counting on means you add numbers and move forward. Counting back means you take away numbers and move backward.
asks: What is the opposite of counting up?

faq.q: Can I use this on a number line if the numbers are big?
faq.a: Yes, you can use it with bigger numbers. Just make sure your number line goes high enough for you to hop to.
asks: What if I go past twenty?

faq.q: Do I have to start at one every time?
faq.a: No, you can start at any number you like. The starting number is very important for your hops.

faq.q: If I count back zero, what happens?
faq.a: If you count back zero, you stay exactly where you started. You do not move at all.
asks: What if I hop back zero steps?
Does hopping zero times change the number?

faq.q: Is there a rule for how many times I can hop?
faq.a: You can hop any number of times. Just count carefully each time you take a step.
asks: Is there a limit to hopping?

facts: Counting on means adding numbers together.
You must start at the correct number.
Each hop moves you by the same amount.

quiz.say: Start at 3 and hop on 4. What number do you land on?
quiz.why: You start at three and take four hops forward: four, five, six, seven.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you subtracted instead of adding.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you added the numbers without counting the hops.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you only hopped three times.

quiz.say: Start at 11 and hop back 3. What number do you land on?
quiz.why: You start at eleven and hop back three times: ten, nine, eight.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only hopped twice.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you put the numbers together instead of subtracting.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you counted on instead of counting back.

quiz.say: If you are at 6 and hop on 5, what is your final number?
quiz.why: You count on five times: seven, eight, nine, ten, eleven.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you counted back instead of counting on.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you put the numbers side by side.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only hopped four times.
